en: A state that is neither a cause nor dissociated from a cause, and is unwholesome, is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a wholesome state that is both a cause and associated with a cause. There are nine [conditions]: object, predominance, and decisive support.

A state that is neither a cause nor dissociated from a cause, and is unwholesome, is a condition, by way of object-condition, for an unwholesome state that is both a cause and associated with a cause. There are nine [conditions]: object, predominance, and decisive support.

A state that is neither a cause nor dissociated from a cause and is not indeterminate (na-abyākata) is related to a state that is both a cause and associated with a cause and is indeterminate by way of the object-condition (ārammaṇa-paccaya). ... [Three.
Nine [ways] by way of object, predominance, proximity, contiguity, and decisive support; three by way of kamma; nine by way of absence and disappearance.
